==English== ===Etymology 1=== {{etymon|en|id=preposition|:inh|enm:wiþ}} From {{inh|en|enm|with}}, from {{inh|en|ang|wiþ|t=against, opposite, toward, with}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*wiþi}}, a shortened form of {{der|en|gem-pro|*wiþrą|t=against}}. In Middle English, the word shifted to denote association rather than opposition, displacing {{cog|enm|mid|t=with}}, from {{cog|ang|mid|t=with}}, from {{cog|gem-pro|*midi}}; an earlier model of this meaning shift exists in cognate {{der|en|non|við}}; elsewhere, the converse meaning shift is exemplified by {{cog|sem-srb|-}} {{m|inm|𐩨𐩺𐩬|t=between, amid}} spawning {{cog|sem-srb|-}} {{m|inm|𐩨𐩬|t=against}} and even likewise frequent reverse meaning {{m|inm|𐩨𐩬|t=from}}. The adverb sense is probably a [[Appendix:Glossary#semantic_loan|semantic loan]] from various other Germanic languages, such as {{semantic loan|en|de|mit|notext=1}}, {{semantic loan|en|no|med|notext=1}}, and {{semantic loan|en|sv|med|notext=1}}.Kaplan, Aidan (2015) “Come with” in the ''Yale Grammatical Diversity Project: English in North America''[http://ygdp.yale.edu/phenomena/come-with], accessed on 2024-05-08. Updated by Tom McCoy (2015) and Katie Martin (2018). ====Alternative forms==== * {{alter|en|wyth|whith}} {{qualifier|obsolete}} * {{sense|abbreviations}} {{l|en|wth|wth}}, {{l|en|wt|wt}} {{qualifier|obsolete}}; He leapt along the corridor in a panic, stopping by the long-case clock at the end where he flattened himself against the wall.}} #* {{quote-journal|en|date=2013-06-21|author=w:Oliver Burkeman|volume=189|issue=2|page=48|magazine=w:The Guardian Weekly|url=http://www.theguardian.com/technology/2013/may/10/conscious-computing-twitter-facebook-google|title=Conscious computing: how to take control of your life online|passage=The dirty secret of the internet is that all this distraction and interruption is immensely profitable. But the real way to build a successful online business is to be better than your rivals at undermining people's control of their own attention.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20210411191513/https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2013/may/10/conscious-computing-twitter-facebook-google}} # In [[support]] of. {{attention|en|redundant to [[be with#English]]?}} #: {{ux|en|We are '''with''' you [[all the way]].}} # [[in regard to|In regard to]]. #: {{ux|en|There are [[a number of]] problems '''with''' your plan.}} #: {{ux|en|[[what on Earth|What on Earth]] is wrong '''with''' my keyboard?}} #: {{ux|en|He was [[pleased]] '''with''' the outcome.}} #: {{ux|en|I’m upset '''with''' my father.}} #* {{RQ:Economist|date=2013-06-29|volume=407|issue=8842|page=72–3|title=[http://www.economist.com/news/international/science-and-technology/21580133-how-microbes-promote-liver-cancer-overweight-punch-gut A punch in the gut]|passage=Mostly, the microbiome is beneficial. It helps '''with''' digestion and enables people to extract a lot more calories from their food than would otherwise be possible. Research over the past few years, however, has implicated it in diseases from atherosclerosis to asthma to autism.}} # {{lb|en|obsolete}} To denote the accomplishment of cause, means, instrument, etc; – sometimes equivalent to {{m|en|by}}. #: {{co|en|slain '''with''' robbers}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Winter's Tale|V|ii|passage=He was torn to / pieces '''with''' a bear:}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1669|author=w:Nathaniel Morton|title=New England’s Memorial |passage=He was sick and lame of the scurvy, so as he could but lie in the cabin-door, and give direction, and, it should seem, was badly assisted either '''with''' mate or mariners}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1721|author=John Mortimer|title=The Whole Art of Husbandry|page=61|passage=But several sowing of Wheat at that time, because 'twas the usual time of doing of it, it lay in the Ground till Rain came, which was the latter end of ''October'' first, and then but part of it came up neither, because it was mustied and spoiled '''with''' lying so long in the Ground {{...}}}} # {{sid|en|using}} Using as an instrument; [[by means of]]. #: {{co|en|cut '''with''' a knife}} #: {{ux|en|I [[water]] my plants '''with''' this [[watering can]]. I have nothing left to buy groceries ('''with''').}} #* {{RQ:Beaumont Fletcher Comedies and Tragedies|A King and no King|IV|passage=you have paid me equal, Heavens, / And sent my own rod to correct me '''with'''}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1620|author={{w|William Bradford}}.|title=Of Plymouth Plantation|url=http://narcissus.umd.edu:8080/eada/html/display.jsp?docs=bradford_history.xml&action=show |passage=They had cut of his head upon the cudy of his boat had not the man reskued him '''with''' a sword,}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1677|author=w:William Wycherley|title=The plain-dealer|section=Prologue |passage=And keep each other company in spite, / As rivals in your common mistress, fame, / And '''with''' faint praises one another damn;}} # {{lb|en|obsolete}} Using as nourishment; more recently replaced by [[on]]. #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Measure|IV|iii|passage=I am fain to dine and sup '''with''' water and bran.}} # Having, owning. #: {{ux|en|It was small and bumpy, '''with''' a tinge of orange.}} #: {{ux|en|There are lots of people '''with''' no homes after the wildfire.}} # Affected by (a certain emotion or condition). #: {{ux|en|Speak '''with''' confidence.}} #: {{ux|en|He spoke '''with''' sadness in his voice.}} #: {{ux|en|John is a person '''with''' multiple sclerosis.}} # Prompted by (a certain emotion). #: {{co|en|[[overcome]] '''with''' happiness}} #: {{co|en|[[green with envy|green '''with''' envy]]; flushed '''with''' success}} # In the [[employment]] of. #: {{ux|en|She was '''with''' Acme for twenty years before retiring last fall.}} # [[considering|Considering]]; [[taking into account]]. #: {{syn|en|given|}} #: {{ux|en|'''With''' your kind of body size, you shouldn’t be eating pizza at all.}} # [[keep up|Keeping up with]]; [[understanding]]; [[follow along|following along]]. #: {{ux|en|That was a lot to explain; are you still '''with''' me?}} #* {{quote-journal|en|date=May 1983|journal=Field & Stream|title=The Lightweight Division|author=David E.
